paragraphs: A spoil heap is a shape made by machinery rather than by nature: material tipped from a height forms a cone at the angle the soil happens to stand at, with tracks up one side and a flattened top where a loader has worked. That angle of repose is what makes a pile read as loose earth rather than as a hill.
It is built in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which lets a soil material tile across the surface without stretching over the slope.

At $19 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits construction and site visualisation, landscaping and groundworks presentation, terrain and environment scenes, agricultural material and games. On sale since 2025.

A three hole balaclava leaves the eyes and mouth open and covers everything else, which produces one of the most instantly readable silhouettes in film and games. The knit gathers around each opening, and the fabric pulls tight over the skull while sagging slightly at the jaw.
The mesh is light at 6,300 polygons and 6,364 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the opening edges where the knit doubles over.

At $19 it suits character set dressing for film, television and games, winter sports and outdoor clothing visualisation, security and tactical material, and retail renders. Real-world scale is kept, so it fits a standard head. On sale since 2022.

A pin flag is a thin fibreglass pole with a numbered flag near the top and a ferrule at the bottom that seats into the hole cup. The flag hangs rather than flies most of the time, and the number on it is what tells a player which green they are looking at from across a course.
The mesh is light at 6,165 polygons and 6,173 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 4 texture maps at 2048x2048 carrying the fabric and the printed number.
At $19 it suits golf course and sports visualisation, broadcast graphics, resort and hospitality renders, sports advertising and games. On sale since 2015.

A shark tooth is a triangle with serrated edges and a broad root, and the serrations are what do the work: they saw rather than pierce. The enamel is smooth and the root is porous and matt, which gives the object two quite different surfaces meeting at a clear line.
The mesh is minimal at 1,090 polygons and 1,092 vertices, built entirely from quads with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 4 texture maps carrying the enamel, the root and the serration detail.

At $19 and built to StemCell specification, it suits natural history and museum visualisation, marine biology and education material, collector and jewellery renders, documentary work and games. On sale since 2019.

A blade dryer works by scraping water off rather than evaporating it, which is why the design is a slot rather than a nozzle and why the machine sits at hand height instead of above a basin. The shape follows that: a flat wall unit with a narrow aperture and no visible controls at all.
The mesh is minimal at 3,074 polygons and 3,153 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 5 texture maps at 4096x4096 carrying the moulded finish and the aperture detail.

At $19 it suits commercial washroom and interior visualisation, facility and hygiene marketing, hospitality and public building scenes, film and television set dressing, and games. On sale since 2020.

A cosmetic laser pen is deliberately designed to look unthreatening: a smooth white cylinder about the size of a marker, with a small display, a plus and minus for intensity and a fine tip. That reassuring form is the whole product design brief for a device people use on themselves at home.
The mesh is minimal at 3,520 polygons and 3,678 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the tip, the button panel and the display recess.

At $19 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits beauty and personal care device marketing, e-commerce and retail renders, cosmetic and dermatology material, bathroom interiors and games. On sale since 2025.

A foil balloon is not inflated like a rubber one. It is two sheets welded around the edge, so it puffs into a pillow shape rather than a sphere, and the seam stays visible as a flat lip all the way round. The metallised surface then reflects the whole room, which is half the effect.
The mesh is light at 11,024 polygons and 5,527 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the puffed panels and the welded edge.
At $19 it suits party and event visualisation, celebration and greeting card imagery, retail and e-commerce renders, interior set dressing and games. On sale since 2023.

House slippers have no structure at all: a soft sole, an open back and an upper that collapses when nobody is wearing them. That collapse is the modelling problem, because a slipper holding a rigid shoe shape looks like footwear rather than like something kicked off by a bed.

The model is built with subdivision geometry at 556 polygons and 600 vertices with non-overlapping UVs, which is remarkably light and exactly right: subdivision keeps the soft forms smooth without carrying the polygon cost.

At $19 and built to StemCell specification, it suits interior and bedroom visualisation, homeware and footwear retail renders, lifestyle and hospitality imagery, e-commerce material and games. On sale since 2021.

A traditional ice bag is a rubberised pouch with a wide screw cap, so it can be opened to take cubes and sealed without leaking. Filled, it sags into a soft disc that conforms to a joint, which is exactly what it is for and what distinguishes it from a rigid cold pack.
It is built with clean surfaces so the rubberised fabric and the metal cap can each take their own material, and the filled form is what carries the realism rather than surface detail.
At $19 it suits medical and first aid visualisation, sports injury and physiotherapy material, clinic and home care scenes, healthcare advertising and games. On sale since 2023.

A dial combination padlock has a rotating face with numbers around it and a shackle that releases when the internal wheels line up. The dial is the whole interface, and it is why these locks are used where keys get lost - lockers, gates, sheds - rather than where security is critical.

The mesh is light at 8,521 polygons and 8,641 vertices in quads and tris. The UVs overlap, sensible on a symmetrical body with a repeating dial pattern, and the StemCell build means it works in a real-time engine.
At $19 it suits security product visualisation, hardware retail and catalogue renders, locker room and storage scenes, workshop and gym interiors, and games. On sale since 2026.

A coffee capsule is a small truncated cone in coloured aluminium with a foil lid crimped over the wide end and a fluted rim. The colour is the flavour code, the flutes are what the machine grips, and the whole object exists in enormous numbers - which is why it has become a design icon in its own right.
The mesh is minimal at 1,556 polygons and 1,607 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which suits a small object whose realism comes from the anodised metal and the printed lid.

At $19 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits coffee and beverage packaging visualisation, brand and label mockups, kitchen and cafe interiors, retail and e-commerce renders, and games. On sale since 2025.

Candy floss is spun sugar wound onto a stick, and its whole character is that it looks solid and is almost entirely air. The surface has to be irregular and slightly translucent at the edges, with visible strand structure rather than a smooth mass, or it reads as insulation foam.
The mesh is light at 12,120 polygons and 8,960 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the irregular outer form and the stick.

A blue version sits on this page at the same $19. Both suit fairground and carnival visualisation, food and confectionery advertising, children's and family imagery, event scenes and games. Built to StemCell specification, on sale since 2023.

A spirits bottle is judged on its shoulder and its neck taper, because that profile is the brand's signature long before a label is readable. Dark glass adds another problem: it hides the contents, so all of the reading is done by the silhouette and by the light along the edges.

The model is built with subdivision geometry at 6,361 polygons and 6,330 vertices with non-overlapping UVs, which suits glassware where the surface has to stay perfectly smooth at any camera distance.
At $19 it suits beverage advertising, bar and restaurant interiors, packaging and label mockups, retail and e-commerce renders, and games. On sale since 2021.

A stick electrode is a steel rod coated in flux with a short bare section at one end for the holder. The flux coating is what does most of the work, shielding the weld pool as it burns off, and the printed classification on it tells a welder exactly what it is for.
The mesh is minimal at 1,396 polygons and 1,416 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which is right for a subject that is essentially a cylinder with a printed marking.
At $19 it suits welding and fabrication visualisation, industrial and trade equipment marketing, workshop scenes, vocational training material and games. On sale since 2021.
